system: You are an equity research assistant at a brokerage. Analysts use your summaries to decide quickly whether a news item matters for a specific stock. Accuracy matters more than completeness: never state anything the article does not support.
prompt:
Target stock: JPMorgan Chase (JPM)

<article>
HEADLINE: US STOCKS-Wall Street futures decline ahead of big bank earnings

BODY:
(For a Reuters live blog on U.S., UK and European stock markets, click or type LIVE/ in a news window.)

*

Results from Citigroup, Bank of America, Wells Fargo expected

*

Midcaps and smallcaps indexes outperform largecap S&P 500

*

Fed speeches may provide clues on future rate trajectory

*

Futures down: Dow 0.17%, S&P 500 0.17%, Nasdaq 0.22%

Jan 14 (Reuters) - U.S. stock index futures dipped on Wednesday as investors braced for earnings from Citigroup, Bank of America and Wells Fargo, while retail sales and producer price data later in the day were expected to offer fresh insight on the health of the economy.

Shares of Bank of America edged higher, while Wells Fargo and Citigroup edged lower in premarket trading ahead of their results. It comes a day after JPMorgan executives warned that a proposed ceiling on credit-card interest rates could severely hurt consumers and drag down financials, hurting financial stocks.

Analysts largely expect U.S. big banks to post a jump in investment banking fees due to a revival in dealmaking.

Wall Street's main indexes have stalled this week after the Dow and the S&P 500 touched record highs, with traders awaiting fourth-quarter earnings to see if they meet elevated expectations.

Analysts project S&P 500 companies will deliver average fourth-quarter earnings growth of 8.8% year-on-year, lifting full-year 2025 bottom-line expansion to 13.2%, according to IBES LSEG data.

At 5:10 a.m. ET, S&P 500 E-minis were down 12.25 points, or 0.17%, Dow E-minis were down 83 points, or 0.17%, and Nasdaq 100 E-minis were down 57.25 points, or 0.22%.

After December's expected consumer-price rise kept rate-cut bets intact for the back half of the year, investors are now watching Wednesday's producer price and retail sales releases, alongside speeches from Fed voting members John Williams, Anna Paulson, Stephen Miran and Neel Kashkari.

Interest rates are expected to stay unchanged for the most part of the first half of 2026, including at the Fed's January meeting, provided inflation and growth remain steady. Traders continue to expect at least two reductions later in the year, LSEG data showed.

Meanwhile, the Danish and Greenlandic foreign ministers will meet with U.S. Vice President JD Vance at the White House later in the day following weeks of threats by President Donald Trump to take control of Greenland, an autonomous territory of Denmark.

So far, markets have largely overlooked geopolitical risks such as the U.S. toppling Venezuela's leader, with enthusiasm around artificial intelligence and fourth-quarter results driving U.S. indexes to new peaks.

The stock market's record rally is also showing early signs of broadening out this year, with S&P 400 midcaps and S&P 600 smallcaps outperforming the largecap S&P 500 so far this year.

Palo Alto Networks and Fortinet fell 3.3% and 2.5%, respectively before the bell after sources told Reuters that Chinese authorities have told domestic companies to stop using some U.S. and Israeli cybersecurity software due to national security concerns. (Reporting by Medha Singh in Bengaluru; Editing by Maju Samuel )
</article>

Instructions:
1. Classify how relevant the article is to JPM:
   - "primary": JPMorgan Chase is the main subject.
   - "secondary": JPMorgan Chase is one of several subjects, or a key driver of the story.
   - "peripheral": JPMorgan Chase is only mentioned in passing.
   - "none": JPMorgan Chase is not mentioned; any link would be your own inference.
2. Use only information stated in the article (headline + body). Do not add background knowledge,
   prices or context that is not in the text. If the body is missing or is generic boilerplate,
   rely on the headline and set "information_quality" to "limited".
3. Keep figures (prices, %, $ amounts, dates) exactly as written. Attribute analyst opinions,
   rumours and "sources say" reports as such.
4. Write for an investor in JPM: the event, the key numbers, and why it could matter for the stock.
   If relevance is "peripheral" or "none", say so plainly and cover only what concerns JPM
   (or, if nothing does, the market context in one sentence). Do not invent a connection.

Return only a JSON object with exactly these keys:
{
  "relevance": "primary" | "secondary" | "peripheral" | "none",
  "event_type": "earnings_guidance" | "analyst_action" | "m_and_a" | "regulatory_legal" | "product_business" | "macro_market" | "management_corporate" | "other",
  "summary": "<= 50 words, focused on JPM",
  "key_facts": ["<= 3 short facts, each <= 15 words, keep figures"],
  "sentiment_for_ticker": "positive" | "negative" | "neutral" | "mixed",
  "sentiment_rationale": "<= 20 words",
  "information_quality": "full" | "limited"
}
